claims.sourceText: Project Winterhaven, full-text search of the 66-page proposal
claims.text: The words 'saucer', 'interceptor', 'Mach' and 'Air Force' do not appear anywhere in the 66-page Project Winterhaven proposal. The description of Winterhaven as proposing a saucer designated a USAF interceptor originates in the 1956 Aviation Studies (International) report, not in the proposal.

claims.locator: biographical sketch bound into the proposal
claims.sourceText: Project Winterhaven, biographical sketch -- a self-description
claims.text: Brown's own biographical sketch bound into Project Winterhaven gives his birth as Zanesville, Ohio, 18 March 1905, and lists Naval Research Laboratory 1930-33, the International Gravity Expedition to the West Indies 1932, Bureau of Ships acoustic and magnetic minesweeping 1940-41, Materials and Processes Engineer at Glenn L. Martin, and radar consultant at Lockheed. Only the Lockheed item is corroborated by a second document, the assignment line of US 2,417,347.
